articles.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI
articles.standfirst: England meekly offer Australia respite from the ongoing sandpaper scandal by being bowled out for 131 in the first one-day international in Perth.

gist: Australia defeated England by seven wickets in the first ODI in Perth.
Mahli Beardman took six wickets for 24 runs on his debut for Australia.
England were bowled out for 131 before Australia comfortably chased down the target.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Australia beat England by seven wickets in the first one-day international in Perth. England were dismissed for 131 in 33.4 overs, with debutant fast bowler Mahli Beardman taking six wickets for 24 runs. Australia reached their target of 132 in 23.3 overs, led by captain Mitchell Marsh, who hit a 29-ball half-century.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The defeat marks England's fourth loss in five matches as they build towards next year's World Cup. Beardman recorded the best figures by an Australian on ODI debut, capitalising on a Perth pitch offering pace and bounce while England's batters made basic errors.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The second match of the three-game series takes place on Sunday in Adelaide.

Rugby.title: France edge past South Africa after thriller in Nations Championship
Rugby.standfirst: France hold their nerve to beat South Africa by just two points, winning 21-19 at the Stade de France, to make it four wins from five in the Nations Championship and putting the home side in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings.

articles.title: France edge past South Africa after thriller in Nations Championship
articles.standfirst: France hold their nerve to beat South Africa by just two points, winning 21-19 at the Stade de France, to make it four wins from five in the Nations Championship and putting the home side in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings.

timeline.text: France hold nerve to edge past South Africa in thriller
France edge past South Africa after thriller in Nations Championship

gist: France defeated South Africa 21-19 at Stade de France.
The victory ended France's five-match losing run against South Africa.
France moved into a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: France scored three first-half tries through Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe, and Louis Bielle-Biarrey. South Africa responded with tries from Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Cobus Reinach, and Malcolm Marx. Despite Jasper Wiese receiving a 20-minute red card, South Africa fought back, but Manie Libbok missed a conversion that would have levelled the game, allowing France to hold on for a 21-19 win.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The result dents South Africa's hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final and puts France in a strong position at the top of the northern hemisphere standings.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: France face Argentina next Saturday, while South Africa face Ireland in Dublin.

fivew: France secured a 21-19 victory against South Africa.
France held on during a thrilling match to end their five-match losing run against South Africa.
